A former translator disclosed witnessing such an interrogation of a detainee in Afghanistan. While the CIA has only confirmed waterboarding for three notable detainees, serious concerns linger about the safety of the torture documentation. Investigations into these practices are ongoing, revealing more about the use of recorded methods during interrogations.

title: 'Very strange': Zelenskyy questions Trump's Putin bonhomie, US support for Ukraine

He expressed disappointment over Trump's positive remarks about Putin while Ukraine faces ongoing conflict. In contrast, Trump described Putin as a friend who genuinely seeks to end the war, revealing the complexities both leaders face in resolving this crisis.

title: Jensen Huang and wife’s foundation gains $2.3B in a day, they have donated $425M

The foundation's philanthropic endeavors have included noteworthy contributions to institutions like Vanderbilt University, positioning charitable giving as a means for strategic investment in future tech innovations. Despite this success, it maintains a low profile in public awareness.

title: 'Wish Akhilesh spent 6 months in jail': Azam Khan quips; gets witty reply from SP chief

During the launch of the SP manifesto for the upcoming elections, Khan shared his emotional turmoil over being distanced from his son and the sleepless nights spent worrying about his son's fate amid transfers.

title: Ohio lawyer denied partnership wins $2m discrimination award after 9-year suit
description: In a landmark ruling, Pamela Pantages, a lawyer from Ohio, has triumphed in her discrimination lawsuit against her previous employer. The Eighth District Court of Appeals upheld a $2 million jury award, affirming her allegations of being denied partnership due to age and gender bias, as noted in the firm's owner’s comments. This decision corroborates the jury's findings of sex discrimination and contract breaches at The Becker Law Firm.

title: Streak broken! Siraj's six-year run comes to an end as India drop him again
description: Mohammed Siraj's impressive run of playing in all away Test series has come to a halt as he was not selected for the playing XI. Since his introduction to the team in 2020, he had always been a part of these matches until now. With Jasprit Bumrah and other key bowlers back, the selectors chose to include Gurnoor Brar, who is making his Test debut.

title: Taj Mahal marble slab taken by East India Company officer to be auctioned in London
description: A remarkable piece of history, a marble slab from the iconic Taj Mahal, is scheduled to be auctioned on December 9 in the UK. This exquisite slab was taken over 200 years ago by Colonel Pownoll Phipps during the British Raj and was recently uncovered during restoration works. Adorned with delicate carvings and semi-precious stones, it mirrors the floral motifs found on Shah Jahan's cenotaph.

title: SC cracks whip on banks over prosecution of officials in homebuyer fraud cases
description: The Supreme Court has demanded that HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital, and PNB Home Finance provide unconditional sanctions. These sanctions involve officials implicated in collusion with builders in housing fraud schemes. The banks' CMDs must articulate their non-compliance in court if not met within a week. CBI’s investigations have led to chargesheets, and trials will commence once the necessary sanctions are secured, underscoring the urgency for timely judicial processes.

title: Father-son team in South Africa sets 408mph record with 3D-printed drone
description: On December 11, 2025, Mike and Luke Bell shattered records by piloting their Peregreen V4 quadcopter to an astonishing average speed of 408.60 mph, making it the fastest battery-powered quadcopter in history. This remarkable achievement resulted from their dedication to innovative design and rigorous testing, employing advanced aerodynamics and cutting-edge 3D printing techniques. It is a monumental step forward in the realm of drone racing.

title: Odisha women turn banana waste into 21,000 festival boats and extra income
description: Odisha's vibrant Boita Bandana festival will witness a creative surge as local women weave miniature boats from banana stems. Supported by around 40 to 50 Self-Help Group members, this innovative project offers a new income stream for the artisans and nearby banana farmers alike. With 21,000 boats on the docket, they're also answering the local government's push to favor eco-friendly materials against plastic options.

title: Court upholds order to move utility pole after years-long neighbour dispute
description: A Connecticut appeals court has upheld an order requiring neighbours to authorise the removal of a utility pole that has blocked two homeowners from widening their driveway, ending a legal dispute that began in 2019.

title: Bihar move illegal, says Supreme Court, quashes premature release of former MP
description: In a significant ruling, the Supreme Court has annulled the Bihar government's controversial decision to release Anand Mohan, who was serving time for murder. The state's attempt to modify prison regulations for his early exit was found unconstitutional. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu criticized the justification threshold for such a change, ultimately mandating that Anand Mohan must surrender within a month.

title: UK net migration tumbles by 92%; Indians still most common nationality to immigrate
description: Long-term international net migration to the UK has seen a sharp decline, reducing to 77,000 for the year ending June 2026, a staggering drop of 92% from the previous peak of 944,000. This reduction is mainly attributed to changes in visa policies that have impacted non-EU immigration, alongside fewer asylum seekers this year. Notably, Indian immigrants accounted for the largest demographics involved in both immigration and emigration.

title: Patrick Mahomes enjoys family time with Brittany and children ahead of Bills showdown
description: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes take out time for their children ahead of the clash against Buffalo Bills.

title: Delhi high court nixes order to cancel NGO’s FCRA licence
description: In a pivotal decision, the Delhi High Court has ruled in favor of the Socio Legal Information Centre, restoring its FCRA licence that was previously annulled by the Home Ministry. The court indicated that there was a lack of evidence to support accusations of the NGO's anti-government actions. Moreover, the court deemed the assertions of the NGO negatively impacting India's image on the global stage as without merit.

title: Judicial member must on bench to confirm PMLA attachment, says Supreme Court
description: The Supreme Court has ruled that a judicial member must be present in the bench deciding asset attachments. This decision focuses on ensuring legal objectivity in the proceedings related to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The ruling addresses the competence of administrative members in handling questions of law and conflicting judgments. The judgment is applicable prospectively and does not allow reopening of past decisions.

title: Opposition worried, feels government won’t risk another defeat

As uncertainty looms, there are rising concerns among opposition parties about the potential impact on their voting power. The DMK, having previously opposed similar measures, now adopts a cautious stance. In contrast, Congress leaders maintain confidence, even as the government's influence grows.

title: Jadeja, Siraj left out yet again! Gurnoor makes Test debut as India opt to bowl

Gurnoor Brar debuted in the Test format, stepping in for Prasidh Krishna in the playing XI. Meanwhile, New Zealand opted to keep their lineup intact following a drawn first Test. This match is critical as both teams strive for a decisive victory.

title: 7 months on, mediation in Sunjay Kapur case hits deadlock
description: Mediation efforts between Rani Kapur and Priya Sachdev Kapur over Sunjay Kapur's estate ended without resolution. Former Chief Justice DY Chandrachud, who mediated the dispute, reported reaching an impasse. Despite 15 sessions aimed at settlement, both parties did not show flexibility or understanding. The Supreme Court noted that no settlement can be forced upon unwilling parties. The court decided to close the mediation process and will issue a ruling soon.

title: Supreme Court raps MNCs for ‘double standard’ on food quality
description: The Supreme Court addressed concerns regarding the quality of food products offered by multinational companies in India. It emphasized the need for uniform standards across different countries to protect Indian consumers. The court directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to enforce strict labeling regulations. Companies must not alter product compositions or conceal ingredient information. This ruling aims to ensure consumer health and transparency in labeling practices.

title: No content from Pakistan to be shown in India, government reminds Netflix
description: In a move reflecting ongoing tensions, the Indian Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has urged Netflix to limit access to Pakistani content, particularly an upcoming series set to debut on December 4. This action follows previous advisories related to national security concerns amid the India-Pakistan conflict. Netflix has not clarified the series' availability in India, as industry groups pursue legal actions against Pakistani media.

title: Pension, insurance for 15 lakh gig workers likely by year-end
description: The government plans to announce a pension scheme and health insurance for gig workers soon. Workers enrolled on the e-Shram portal will be the primary beneficiaries of these initiatives. The National Social Security Board will discuss contributory models, including a 2% turnover-based contribution from platforms. Trade unions have suggested immediate health and accident cover for these workers during onboarding.

title: 'Back door for low-skilled migrants': Reform UK pledges to scrap graduate visa route
description: Reform UK has announced plans to abolish graduate visas, citing concerns about low-skilled migration. These visas allow international students to work in the UK for two years after completing their degrees. Additionally, the party aims to introduce stricter rules for international students seeking to remain in the country. Reform UK has received criticism for targeting international students, particularly those from India.

title: Supreme Court sets timer for FSSAI, companies to implement warning labels
description: The Supreme Court has instructed the FSSAI to implement front-of-package labeling within four months. Companies will have one year to comply with these regulations after the notification. Labels will indicate high levels of sugar, saturated fat, and salt inside red hexagonal shapes to protect consumer health. The court emphasized the importance of preventing public health crises associated with unhealthy food consumption.

title: Gukesh's berlin defence masterclass holds Sindarov to draw in game 3
description: In a gripping clash at the World Chess Championship, D Gukesh showcased impressive strategy with black pieces, managing a hard-fought draw against Javokhir Sindarov. After 60 intense moves, both competitors stood at 1.5 points. Gukesh's adept use of the Berlin Defence successfully thwarted Sindarov's aggressive tactics. Following a well-deserved rest day, the players gear up for Game 4, where Gukesh will shift to white, keeping the championship fiercely contested.

title: Why old ammunition can become a ticking time bomb: The science behind controlled explosions
description: A controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of lead azide was carried out successfully in Iowa. This explosive compound had deteriorated and posed risks to public safety over the years. Residents expressed concerns about potential health and environmental hazards from the planned blast. The US Army confirmed that the risks had been reduced to near zero after the operation.

They allege that this move aims to secure the necessary numbers for the delimitation-linked Constitution amendment Bill. Various opposition parties have expressed concerns about the implications for parliamentary democracy. The Congress and CPI(M) particularly highlight the government’s motives behind this political maneuvering.

title: Ex-terrorist fugitive’s 19-year run ends in arrest
description: Mohammad Mansha, a former terrorist, was arrested by a joint police team in Tral. He had evaded law enforcement for nearly two decades since laying down arms in 2007. Authorities revealed he was wanted in at least 13 criminal cases, including murder and conspiracy. His criminal activities included the killing of a police officer back in 2000. The operation involved meticulous planning and credible intelligence from various police units.

title: Germany assures India of sensitive tech transfer in $9bn submarine deal
description: Germany's commitment to technology transfer under the P-75I submarine project with India is being emphasized. This partnership aims to enhance India's capabilities in undersea warfare technology, including Air-Independent Propulsion. Both nations share mutual trust regarding the protection of sensitive technologies and strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region. The deal may also lead India to become a hub for submarine manufacturing for Southeast Asian nations.

Sunni scholar Maulana Abdul Rashid Dawoodi urged for a fatwa regarding standing during its rendition. Meanwhile, grand mufti Nasir-ul-Islam declared participation as impermissible under Islamic law. Several clerics expressed regret after attending a function where Vande Mataram was played. The controversy stems from a recent Union home ministry directive mandating its performance at official events.

title: 30 missing ultras working from Pakistan & PoK to revive terrorism in J&K: Police

They obtained training and arms to launch activities against India while disrupting peace in Jammu and Kashmir. These individuals are now associated with Hizbul Mujahideen, facilitating the supply of arms and funds. Police have registered an FIR against them under various laws, including the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

title: Road min tightens bidding norms to keep poor performers out of govt projects
description: The road transport ministry has updated the bidding process for contractors to ensure better project execution. Performance ratings will now determine contractors’ eligibility for new projects, replacing the old financial year assessment approach. Stricter norms for joint ventures and improved technical eligibility conditions for major infrastructure projects have also been implemented. The revised Request for Proposal framework emphasizes transparency by requiring bidders to disclose ongoing disputes.

This Bill aims to provide 33 percent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies. The Constitution amendment aims to increase Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850, linking it to delimitation. His partnership with Chetan Sakariya yielded an impressive 62 runs for the 10th wicket.
